What is depreciation?

options.A: a means of allocating the cost of a non-current asset over its useful life
options.B: a measure of the decrease in market value of a non-current asset
options.C: an outflow of cash from the use of a non-current asset
options.D: the expense spent on the non-current asset

A full year’s charge for depreciation is made in every year of use. After four years the asset was sold. The loss on disposal was $30000 and disposal costs were $10000. What were the sale proceeds?

options.A: interest charged on overdue accounts of customers

questions.questionText: A trader prepared a trial balance which did not balance. The difference was posted to a suspense account. The following errors have now been found.
How could a credit entry of $500 in X’s account have arisen in the books of account of Y?

options.C: Y made a payment to X.

questions.questionText: An invoice for purchases was credited to the purchases account. How will the balance on the purchases account be corrected?

options.A: decrease by the value of the invoice
options.B: decrease by twice the value of the invoice
options.C: increase by the value of the invoice
options.D: increase by twice the value of the invoice

questions.questionText: Rent is paid by a business monthly in advance on the first day of each month. The payments during a financial year were as follows. up to and including 1 June $500 per month from 1 July $600 per month Which amounts will appear in the financial statements for the year ended 31 October? statement of financial income statement position
What is the effect on profit for the year and net assets when accrued expenses are understated? profit for the year net assets

Ali’s trade receivables at 31 December 2019 were $26500. He knew that $400 of these were irrecoverable. He wished to maintain a provision for doubtful debts equal to 5% of the trade receivables. At 1 January 2019 the balance of the provision for doubtful debts was $1200. Which entry does Ali make in the provision for doubtful debts account at 31 December 2019?

Adil and Bashir were in partnership sharing profits and losses in the ratio 2:1. Chandra joins the partnership and profits and losses are now to be shared between Adil, Bashir and Chandra in the ratio 3:2:1. The balances of the partners’ capital accounts prior to Chandra joining the partnership are as follows: $ Adil 20000 Bashir 10000 Goodwill is to be valued at $36000 and is not to be retained in the books of account. What is the balance on Adil’s capital account after Chandra joined the partnership?
How is a loss on realisation recorded when a partnership is dissolved?

options.A: Credit each partner’s capital account equally.
options.B: Debit each partner’s capital account equally.
options.C: Credit each partner’s capital account in the profit-sharing ratio.
options.D: Debit each partner’s capital account in the profit-sharing ratio.

questions.questionText: John and Brian are in partnership sharing profits and losses equally. John receives a salary of $2000 per annum. Brian loaned the business $5000. What will be the amount of residual profit Brian will receive for the year?
